title: operator: implicit Helm values overriding customer node-affinity during onprem upgrade — revertible hotfix
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Summary: Several customers running private/VPC deployments observed nodes losing scheduled workloads following the 2026.03 operator upgrade. Investigation shows the operator helm chart started applying an implicit default nodeAffinity stanza when CRDs were reconciled, which overwrote customer-specified affinities stored in on-cluster helm values. This caused pods to be evicted or remain Pending in clusters with strict node selectors, leading to customer escalations and PagerDuty alerts.

Scope: Affects on-prem and VPC customers using operator versions 2026.03.0 and 2026.03.1 with pre-existing custom helm values that include nodeAffinity/nodeSelector. Hosted and Dedicated are not affected.

Impact: Multiple customers reported degraded control-plane (operator) availability and downstream service outages, some required manual rollback to previous operator version. Immediate mitigation and a revertible hotfix are required to prevent further customer impact and to restore cluster schedules without forcing full manual upgrades for customers with strict scheduling constraints.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Install operator v2026.03.0 on a cluster with a custom helm values file that sets spec.controller.nodeAffinity for the runtime pods.
2) Trigger a CRD reconciliation (e.g., update an unrelated annotation on the OperatorConfig CR).

3) Observe that reconciler rewrites the effective helm values: operator reconciler merged default affinity and replaced cluster-stored affinity with chart default, resulting in pods Pending or evicted on clusters with strict labels.
4) Inspect operator logs: "reconciling values: applying defaults for nodeAffinity" and sample K8s events showing FailedScheduling due to nodeSelector mismatch.
root_cause: During refactor to centralize Helm chart defaults (RFC #OP-142), an aggressive values-merge was implemented where chart defaults were deep-merged into stored release values during every reconcile cycle. The merge strategy used 'overwrite' semantics for affinity blocks instead of 'preserve existing' semantics. This caused customer-provided affinity/nodeSelector blocks to be silently replaced on reconcile. The regression was not caught by existing upgrade/integration tests because most CI clusters use permissive node labels.
mitigation:
1) Opened emergency branch to change merge strategy to 'preserve' for affinity/nodeSelector blocks and added an explicit opt-out flag (respectExistingAffinity=true).
2) Issued step-by-step rollback guidance for impacted customers: downgrade operator to 2026.02.x and re-apply their stored helm values.
3) Temporary admission: disable automatic reconcile for OperatorConfig (patch annotation 'redwood.io/auto-reconcile: "false"') for clusters under active incident until hotfix deploys.
proposed_hotfix:
- Code: change chart-values merge to prefer cluster-stored affinity when keys exist and add unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/674 (draft).
- Release: operator-2026.03.2-hotfix build (image-tag sha256:abcd1234hotfix).
- Backout: hotfix includes a safe rollback path (helm rollback + crd reconcile script) and healthchecks to verify pod schedules before marking rollout complete.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1 (canary): deploy hotfix to internal staging + 2 low-impact customer clusters (03/13) with manual verification of schedule and controller logs.
Stage 2: 50% of affected clusters (selected by region/policy) with automated monitoring for 60 minutes.
Stage 3: full customer-wide rollout with 10-minute pause windows and automatic rollback if SLOs breach.
Communication: send targeted customer notification and coordinated window with SRE and SE teams.
monitoring_and_validation:
- Verify no pods enter Pending with message 'node(s) didn't match node selector' for 15 minutes post-upgrade.
- Validate operator logs contain no 'applying defaults for nodeAffinity' messages.
- Dashboard: private-deployments/scheduling-errors (alert threshold > 5 clusters in 30m).
- Smoke checks: run kube-scheduler e2e schedule test harness included in rollout job.

postmortem_tasks: 1) Add integration test scenarios with strict node labels and non-default affinities to upgrade CI pipeline (owner: eng-infra).
2) Add audit log entry when operator modifies affinity blocks (owner: runtime-team).
3) Update operator chart README to document which keys are considered sensitive and preserved on reconcile (owner: docs).
4) Review RFC #OP-142 merge semantics and add a checklist for 'merge-impact' for future refactors (owner: arch).
